headline: Vancouver Canucks trade Aatu Räty to Toronto Maple Leafs for 2 depth forwards
take:
The Athletic reports that the Canucks have traded Aatu Räty to the Maple Leafs for two depth forwards, noting he had one goal in four games for Vancouver this season.

The numbers suggest Toronto is getting a small, uncertain piece. Räty's own expected goals (a measure of the quality of the chances he generates) so far this season come to 0.96, almost exactly his one goal, so there is no hidden scoring luck to bet on. At 5-on-5 his team had just 28.1 percent of the expected goals when he played, and Vancouver did 11.75 percentage points better with him off the ice, though four games is a tiny sample. He averaged only 10.16 minutes a game, and last season he managed four goals and 14 points in 66 games. Toronto sits at 5-4-2 with a 46.6 percent expected goal share, and a depth forward alone won't fix that. For Vancouver (2-8-1, 38.5 percent expected goal share, goals saved above expected of -7.9), this trade changes little. Fantasy managers can leave Räty on the wire.
